A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same REPA study, with complete main text and Appendices A–M. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the equations, tables, figures, and appendix material.

before.justification: v3 reports original REPA experiments, representation analyses, and ablations, including ImageNet generation and MS-COCO text-to-image results in Section 4 and Appendices J–L.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the main experiments, appendix benchmark evaluations, and feature-map analyses.

M1.justification: REPA's patch-wise representation alignment, projection MLP, combined training objective in Equations (8)–(9), and model architectures are unchanged. The terminology edits introduce no procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet 256×256 and 512×512 generation tasks, ImageNet representation evaluations, and MS-COCO text-to-image experiments. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main comparisons and appendix Tables 8–12. Appendix F's revised description of SiT as using 'flow matching' does not change the evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, metrics, sampling procedures, and guidance settings are unchanged. This includes the 50,000-sample generation evaluation and default NFE of 250.

E4.justification: The encoder, alignment-depth, objective, regularization-weight, and noise-level analyses are retained unchanged. Appendix analyses of DiT representations, encoder training data, guidance settings, and PCA feature maps also match.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged throughout the text, tables, and plots. Neither revision adds or changes repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are unchanged. Examples include FID 7.9 after 400K iterations without guidance in Table 3, FID 1.42 with guidance scheduling in Table 4, and the MS-COCO results in Table 12.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(24), stochastic-interpolant assumptions, and CKA/CKNNA definitions are unchanged. Appendix A.2's replacement of 'flow-based' with 'flow matching' changes terminology without revising mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about representation learning, REPA, faster convergence, and improved generation quality. The claimed speedup and best FID are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of representation alignment and later layers capturing high-frequency details are unchanged. Appendix M retains the same limitations and future directions concerning alignment depth, other domains, theory, and time-varying regularization.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training speed, preprocessing instructions, and code/checkpoint release information are unchanged. The revised funding acknowledgment adds no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and Section 5 and Appendix I retain the same research positioning. Reference entries move across page breaks without additions or removals.

P1.justification: Section 1 and Appendices A.2 and F replace selected 'flow-based' wording with 'flow matching'. The acknowledgment updates SX's funding attribution and separates paragraphs; the scientific narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 changes the DiT-XL/2 baseline's '7M' iteration entry from bold to regular type, without changing its value. Acknowledgment spacing reflows references across pages 11–17, and the arXiv stamp updates. Figures and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 makes localized terminology and formatting edits and updates funding attribution. REPA, all main-text and appendix evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged. These small editorial adjustments do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
